title: The board
goal: A stroke is a chord: keys down together, released together.

head: Zone
Keys
Job
rows: `S T K P W H R`
`F R P B L G T S D Z`

`+`: left index finger's inner column (`T` and `G` on a keyboard), a tall key between the `H`/`R` column and the star; struck with a stroke to continue a word. `*`: right index finger's tall key, the tiebreaker (lesson 9).

blocks.x: The left pinky's `S-` is one tall key, as in standard steno. `+` and `*` are tall keys too: `+` at the left index finger's inner column, `*` at the right index finger's, so each index finger has two columns. The top bar is the `#` number bar, unused by lyk. Keys are grey until part of a stroke: colour means *held*. The rest are top and bottom pairs; each finger owns a column: top key `T P H` / `F P L T D`, bottom `K W R` / `R B G S Z`.
Strike keys. The label shows the stroke in steno order and, if it is a word, its dictionary entry.

The board draws some co-held keys as one bigger key: `T P H` lights as a single `N`, `P H` as `M`, `A O` as `AO`. Display only; the stroke is the same keys. Full list: [cheat sheet](#/ref/cheatsheet).
Keys are always written in this order, however pressed:

rows: `S T K P W H R`
`F R P B L G T S D Z`

blocks.x: Hence [[PHAP]] is *map*, not *pam*. A letter can sit on both sides (`R`, `P`, `T`, `S`), so a stroke of right-hand keys only, with no vowel, takes a hyphen: [[-T]] is T on the right, [[T]] is T on the left.
Left hand starts the sound, right hand ends it. A word whose sounds come in that order fits in one stroke.

items: Press a stroke's keys at about the same time; order does not matter.
The stroke is sent when **every** key is up.
Hold `T` or `G` (the `+` key, left index finger's inner column) with a stroke for the join key. [[+-G]] is `T` and `L` together: `L` is the right-hand `-G` key.

blocks.q: How is T on the right hand written alone?
blocks.why: The hyphen says: right-hand keys only.

drill.title: Read the stroke, strike it
drill.x: Each prompt is a stroke written the way steno writes it: left hand, then thumbs, then right hand, a dash where it is needed. Strike those keys together, then let go, and see the word you made. The keys light up after a miss. 90% first try passes.
